subject: BrightLane POC: long-session streaming disconnect — triage & MAP
messages:
From: Caroline Patel <caroline@brightlanehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up — streaming disconnect during long-report POC

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We pushed a 45-minute automated report generation job through the POC (using the SDK streaming API) and saw a disconnect after ~28 minutes. The UI showed a "connection reset" and the client had to re-open the stream — we lost the in-flight tokens.

Attached is the client-side session log from our environment (brightlane_report_session.log). We tried increasing the keepalive to 30s on our end with no change. This is a blocker for us because our reports often exceed 30 minutes and we need uninterrupted streaming for progressive rendering.

Can your team triage? Marissa, looping you in for context on contract timelines — we're aiming to close this quarter.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Patel
Head of Data Integrations
BrightLane Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Patel <caroline@brightlanehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up — streaming disconnect during long-report POC

Caroline — thanks for the log and the clear repro notes. I'm sorry you hit this in the POC.

Quick next steps from our side:
- I've routed the session log to Dev (cc'd) for immediate triage.
- Can you confirm the SDK version you used and whether you were using the default prefetch/batching config? A screenshot of the client keepalive and any proxy between your client and our hosted API would help.
- We're going to attempt a repro internally against a matching model + seq_len to see if this is a runtime-side disconnect (connection or streaming framing) or a client-side socket handling bug.

Marissa — FYI on the timeline pressure. If this is a runtime regression we may need a focused canary deploy / hotfix to the POC cluster and a short exception to SLA for BrightLane while we validate.

I'll coordinate and come back with an ETA by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up — streaming disconnect during long-report POC

Thanks for the logs — I reproduced a similar disconnect locally while running the repro script against a 130k-token simulated report (same model config). Initial triage notes: 

Findings:
- The runtime shows a KV-cache flush around 1.2M generated tokens which coincides with the streaming buffer being rotated. At the same time we see a NullPointerException in the streaming frame handler (stack trace attached: runtime-stack-trace.txt).
- The SDK keeps the TCP connection open but the server-side stream handler crashes and the connection resets. This appears to be a runtime-side bug in the path that handles large continuous KV cache growth + prefetch.

Immediate mitigations (recommended):
- BrightLane: reduce client prefetch to 8 (was 32) and enable short prefix caching (ok for progressive rendering) — this avoids triggering the cache rotation in our repro.
- On our side: prepare a targeted canary patch that adds a guard on the streaming frame handler and delays KV cache rotation until in-flight streams finish (low-risk change).

Ask:
- Can we get a POC window to deploy the canary to the BrightLane dedicated cluster (2 hours maintenance window)? I can have a patch candidate and tests by EOD today if we prioritize.

I've attached a minimal repro script (repro-script.sh) and the trimmed stack trace. If anyone else on runtime wants to look I can pair-call.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Platform / Runtime Eng
dev_patel@redwood.com

-M

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: BrightLane POC: proposed MAP + canary schedule

Caroline — thanks for the patience and for the quick repro logs. Concretely: 

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Canary deploy (target): Thu 2026-01-15 10:00–12:00 PT — runtime team (Dev) will deploy a guarded patch to the BrightLane POC cluster and run the repro job with identical load.
2) Client mitigation: BrightLane to set SDK prefetch=8 and keepalive=15s for the test window (we'll provide a one-line patch if needed).
3) Validation: Redwood to stream 3 long-report runs; if no disconnects we roll patch to POC cluster and monitor for 48 hours.
4) Escalation / credits: If disconnect persists after canary, Redwood will open a priority incident (SUP-4532) and consider a one-time credit for lost POC hours.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_BrightLane_v1.docx (MAP), and links to the HubSpot deal + JIRA ticket.

Sergio — can you draft a short customer note to send the morning of the canary outlining the user impact and expectations? Marissa — please confirm the credit boundary (what we can promise if we miss the canary) so I can include it in the MAP.

Caroline — if this schedule works I'll send a calendar invite and an access checklist for the 1/15 window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
